header:
Date: 2026-08-25
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Zhou (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (CISO, Bluehaven), Priya Kapoor (Head of Platform), Ethan Moore (DevOps), Lina Cho (Compliance)
Notes: Security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment, SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, retention
summary: Bluehaven is evaluating Redwood for LLM inference across hosted/dedicated/private. Primary concerns: SOC 2 / ISO coverage, SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC and least-privilege, audit log retention and forwarding to Splunk, KMS BYOK and HSM support, and data residency/retention policy enforcement. Team requested SOC2 report, ISO scope, and a POC plan that includes KMS integration and network diagrams.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, do you want to do quick intros then jump into security posture stuff?
[00:08] Mark: Sure, I'm Mark Reynolds, CISO at Bluehaven, with Priya and Ethan we own infra and platform. Lina from compliance is here too but she's on mute.
[00:17] Priya: Hi, Priya, thanks for taking time. We're evaluating options across hosted, dedicated, or fully private. Main ask is how you handle compliance and key management.
[00:27] Samir: Great. High level, Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. On compliance we are SOC 2 Type II and we have customers using us with ISO27001 requirements - we can share the reports, scope, caveats.
[00:38] Nina: To add, for private deployments we offer a customer-managed control plane option so keys and networking stay in your VPC, and on-prem box variants for air-gapped use.
[00:47] Ethan: When you say keys in VPC, does that mean BYOK with our AWS KMS? We need HSM-backed keys for certain workloads.
[00:53] Samir: Yes BYOK, AWS KMS and GCP KMS are supported; we also support HSM integrations for private deployments. There's a small caveat for hosted: you can do envelope encryption with your KMS where root keys never leave your KMS, we store only wrapped key material.
[01:05] Mark: Can you walk through audit logging? We need full request-level logs forwarded to our SIEM and retention of 7 years for certain records.
[01:12] Nina: We emit structured audit logs - request id, model version, token counts, user id (if provided), route, latencies, errors. For hosted customers we provide log forwarding to Splunk/Datadog/Cloud Logging via customer-managed forwarding; for dedicated/private you can run our logging agents in your VPC and keep logs internally.
[01:27] Priya: Any risk of PHI/PII persistence in your systems for hosted? We need guarantees around data retention and deletion.
[01:34] Samir: Good question; default hosted policy is ephemeral prompt retention for X days (we'll share current default retention), you can opt into zero retention for enterprise tiers or use private deployment which never leaves your network. We also have contractual clauses for data deletion and purge procedures.
[01:47] Mark: We will need contractual SLAs and also auditors will want to see the SOC2 report and the exact retention slides.
[01:53] Samir: We'll send the SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 scope and also a one-pager on retention/legal language.
[01:59] Ethan: About SSO - we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning. Does Redwood support SAML SSO and SCIM for groups/roles?
[02:07] Nina: Yes, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning. For RBAC you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles; for dedicated/private you can enforce IdP-only authentication and disable local accounts.
[02:20] Priya: For RBAC, can we enforce least privilege per model or per route? We need per-environment separation between dev/stage/prod.
[02:27] Samir: Yes roles can be scoped per project/route and you can lock model versions; we support environment-level isolation in Dedicated and Private, and namespaces in hosted enterprise tier.
[02:38] Mark: A couple of other things - we've got regulatory constraints for data residency in EMEA, can Redwood pin regions and ensure no egress?
[02:45] Nina: We route regionally and you can constrain routing by policy; for hosted enterprise we have regional endpoints, and dedicated/private give you full control. For true egress control on hosted you can use dedicated capacity in the EMEA region.
[02:58] Ethan: On encryption at rest and in transit, are all tokens and model weights encrypted? Does plaintext ever touch disk?
[03:04] Samir: All customer data in transit uses TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest, you get envelope encryption; model weights in shared hosted pools are encrypted and access controlled. For private/dedicated you control the keys. We can provide architecture docs for key lifecycle.
[03:18] Priya: About network - do you support private link / VPC peering? We prefer no public endpoints for inference traffic.
[03:24] Nina: Yes, Private supports VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink patterns; Dedicated can be provisioned in your VPC or connected via PrivateLink to avoid public internet. Hosted has regional private endpoints for enterprise customers.
[03:38] Mark: Auditors will ask about change management and deployment traceability - can you provide immutable audit trails for infra changes and who deployed which model/version?
[03:46] Samir: We have deployment audit logs with actor identity, commit hash, rollout type (canary/A-B), and timestamp. For Dedicated/Private customers you can opt-in for longer retention and export to your SIEM.
[03:58] Priya: How about secrets management for runtime - e.g., we have downstream connectors to EHR and need per-request secrets managed securely.
[04:06] Nina: We support runtime secret injection via secure vault integrations; secrets are not logged in plaintext and are only available to the runtime container. For hosted customers we have masked logs and redaction heuristics but for sensitive workloads we recommend private/dedicated with vault integration.
[04:24] Ethan: What's your incident response posture - playbooks, SLA for notification? We need 24h notice for incidents, and root-cause within 72h.
[04:31] Samir: We provide incident notifications to our customers per tier; enterprise SLA includes a 1-hour acknowledgment and an initial incident report within 24 hours, full RCA in 72 hours. We can share our incident response runbook redacted for security.
[04:43] Mark: Do you have penetration test results or bug bounty program details?
[04:47] Nina: We run regular third-party pentests and we have a coordinated vuln disclosure program. We'll share a summary of the last pentest and the bug bounty program page link.
[04:56] Priya: For the POC, we'd like to test a small flow with our redaction + tokenization pipeline, test KMS BYOK, and validate latency on dedicated pool with heavy batching. Can Redwood run the dedicated pool in our VPC for that POC?
[05:08] Samir: Yes, we can spin up a short-lived dedicated pool in your VPC or provide a private deployment sandbox. Nina can scope POC tasks and resource needs.
[05:17] Nina: I'll propose a POC with three parts: 1) KMS BYOK keywrap test, 2) audit log forwarding to Splunk, 3) latency/throughput run with batch sizes representative of your traffic.
[05:28] Mark: Also we need to confirm contractual obligations around data deletion and e-discovery.
[05:33] Samir: We'll include our standard data retention annex and we can add e-discovery obligations into the SOW for enterprise deals.
[05:39] Ethan: Any blockers for us to run a short security review with our auditors? They usually want network diagrams, SOC2 and a pen test summary.
[05:46] Samir: No blockers - we'll send SOC2, ISO scope, pen test summary, and a template network diagram for the POC.
[05:53] Mark: Good. One minor transcription note - sometimes hosted vendor names show wrong in OCR, but that's fine.
[05:59] Samir: Haha, noted. Quick recap then next steps?
[06:02] Nina: Recap: Samir to send SOC2/ISO docs and retention one-pager; Nina to draft POC plan for KMS/audit/latency; Bluehaven to send network diagram and retention constraints.
[06:12] Priya: We'll aim to get the network diagram and the list of regulated stores by Friday.
[06:17] Samir: I'll include pricing ranges for hosted vs dedicated vs private in the follow-up and flag differences for the POC.
[06:23] Mark: Sounds good - thanks everyone.
[06:25] Samir: Thanks - we'll follow up via email with docs and time for the infra deep-dive.
[06:30] (call ends)

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and truncated phrases typical of automated meeting extracts; proper names may be slightly off.
